refined_brief: Source-grounded 4:3 black/white abstracts with framed subfigures, appropriate quantitative plots, explained terminology, consistent spacing and right-aligned source credits.
central_argument: Plastic-hinge deformation images are clustered into labels and classified by logistic regression; the published 88.08 percent test accuracy concerns those cluster-derived labels.
source_evidence: Published Tables 1, 2 and 4 and the methods figures support the image pipeline. The input is a 7 by 8 re-entrant lattice represented by 64 by 64 pixel images. Eight K-means labels C0-C7 precede the KNet1 logistic-regression classifier. Training/validation/testing allocation is 60/20/20 percent. Table 2 test accuracies at learning rates 0.00001, 0.0001 and 0.001 are 46.29, 79.83 and 88.08 percent. Table 4 is described as the end-of-training confusion matrix; its diagonal entries, multiplied by 100, are recorded in class-results.csv. Four of six mechanisms were identified: V, X, V+Z+V and distorted X.
limitations: Table 4 does not explicitly establish which data split its matrix uses. The class-wise dot plot is therefore labeled confusion-matrix diagonal, not held-out class accuracy. The 70-103 percent dot axis is intentionally cropped for comparison; the test-accuracy bars start at zero. Class glyphs are illustrative reconstructions, not source images or measured centroids. Independent deformation-mode ground truth is unavailable. No new training or KNet2 result is implied.
